questions.q: What does an unauthenticated scan have access to?
options: The target's local registry settings and configuration files
Nothing at all — unauthenticated scans produce no findings
Full administrative access to every installed application on the target
Only what's visible over the network without logging in, like open ports and service banners
questions.explain: An unauthenticated scan mirrors an outside attacker's view: open ports, service banners, and whatever is exposed to the network.

questions.q: What does an authenticated scan do differently?
options: Only scans ports that are already known to be closed
Removes the need for any vulnerability database at all
Logs into the target with valid credentials and inspects it from the inside
Runs exclusively on unpatched systems
questions.explain: Authenticated scans use credentials (e.g., over SMB/WinRM or SSH) to log in and see installed software, patch levels, and local config directly.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what did the authenticated scan find on the Windows server that the unauthenticated scan missed?
options: Nothing — both scans reported identical findings
A completely different operating system running on the host
An open port that the unauthenticated scan had also already reported
An outdated PDF reader, missing security updates, and a weakened registry setting
questions.explain: These local issues never touch the network, so only a scan that logs in directly to the host can discover them.

questions.q: What is the real cost of running authenticated scans, according to this lesson?
options: They require disabling the target's firewall entirely
They are always slower than unauthenticated scans by design
Authenticated scans cannot detect missing patches at all
Credential management — maintaining, rotating, and restricting high-privilege scanning accounts
questions.explain: Authenticated scans need broad administrative credentials, which become a high-value target if not managed carefully across many systems.

questions.q: What do most mature vulnerability management programs actually do?
options: Rely exclusively on unauthenticated scans and never use credentials
Skip scanning entirely in favor of manual review
Run authenticated scans only once, at the very start of the program
Run authenticated scans as the primary assessment, with occasional unauthenticated scans to validate the outside view
questions.explain: Authenticated scanning is the thorough, primary method, while unauthenticated scanning still has value for checking the external attacker's view.
